format: UTF-8 JSON Lines, one event per line; finite-width source REAL words are little-endian IEEE-754 raw hex bytes, not decimal approximations.
scope: Original pinned standard executable, one debugger process on the owning rank, normal original executable on seven other ranks, 80 seconds/four KDM calls; no physics or executable changes.

function_entry_return.fields: raw 4-byte words keyed by physical operand name
function_entry_return.metadata: actual bounds, KDM timestep or provisional next KDM timestep, RK or acoustic iteration where available; pointer base addresses, scs/sce checked against runtime P_QNR and spec_zone
function_entry_return.semantics: provisional timestep is counted from previous completed KDM entry; do not infer a finer model timestamp. Source and absolute PC binds require unchanged executable SHA.

entry_fields: scalar_old only after witnessed RK1 for same old-array target
nr_operator.source_semantics: For RK1 the routine first copies scalar_current to scalar_old; numerator uses that copy, not the pre-call scalar_old. Later stages use stored scalar_old. Tendency combines the recorded advection and scalar tendency on source-defined ranges; scalar_tendency is not assumed zero. Actual dt and spec_zone are recorded.
nr_operator.pointer_gate: Each RK event records scs, sce and runtime P_QNR independently; all must agree. KDM6 NR argument must equal the observed QNR scalar slice base each timestep. The breakpoint observes the target scalar element and records changes during this operator, not earlier writers.
nr_operator.initialization: RK1 entry scalar_old is not read; it is recorded after return and later RK entries are accepted only after a witnessed RK1 for the same address.

pressure_operator.initialization: al and p are INTENT(OUT), so pre-call values are not interpreted; pm1 is not read at step 0 and later reads require a witnessed completed step 0 for that exact target pointer. GDB watchpoint setup necessarily samples an opaque old word; the first watch event does not report it. Nonhydrostatic must be true and k+1 inside allocated bounds.
pressure_operator.source_semantics: When step>0, p_final=p_raw+smdiv*(p_raw-pm1_old); pm1_new=p_raw. Input producers earlier than this routine remain unresolved until explicitly traced.

preparation_operator.source_semantics: PF=P+PB and PII=((P+PB)/P0)**RCP; TH is dry theta formed from t_new and qv according to use_theta_m. Do not claim bit-exact source arithmetic until actual instruction/rounding checked.
preparation_operator.pointer_gate: Within each timestep prep p input must equal a preceding calc_p_rho p pointer, and TH, PII and PF outputs must match KDM6 arguments. Pointer identity alone does not prove no intervening writes.

kdm_boundary.timing: Entry and return around the original KDM6 call, first four actual calls. TK is reconstructed for target parity as rounded float32 TH*PII; this is not a separately observed memory field. t=th*pii on ingress and th=t/pii before return are within-call transformations and not external interval E.

watch_after.interpretation: Hardware write watchpoint reports after a changed store; address and actual post-state are observed. The reported PC may be after the store and must not be asserted as the exact writer without independent disassembly and a separately approved pre-instruction replay. Vector-lane inputs are not necessarily recoverable from post-store registers. Zero watch events mean no observed value-changing store and do not establish no stores.

gates: phase0_03 full all-rank global14 and selected16 first-four parity plus h00 passed on the same executable
each job must recheck all 89 inputs, executable and runtime profile before/after, h00 byte equality, and owner-target KDM ENTRY/RETURN parity for all four steps
require all pointer bindings, runtime P_QNR identity, owner/bounds and actual event coverage
no source-only causal attribution, no absence-as-zero, no pre-instruction result claimed from post-watch state
freeze scripts, schema, target and command; independent review and explicit root GO required before execution
